title: The Great Replacement Chronicles: The Mandela Effect
excerpt: Exploring the cultural impact of Nelson Mandela statue in Glasgow and BIPOC representation in Europe.
content:
Archiving the “strange death of Europe,” as Douglas Murray put it, and the West more broadly, at the hands of the neoliberal technocracy

The latest manifestation of the Western social engineers’ fetish for inflicting obscene statues of BIPOCs on the natives occurred in occupied Scotland.

Related: 12-Foot Statue of Obese Black Woman Appears in Times Square

In the most recent moving tribute to globo-homo race communism, the authorities in charge of Glasgow have seen fit to install a gigantic statue of Nelson Mandela — the infamous communist terrorist of South Africa who helped turn it into the failed state that it is today, following in the footsteps of Rhodesia, now known as Zimbabwe — so as to inspire the Deplorable Scottish bigots to commit their own communist takeover.

In true communist fashion, a performance by a women’s drumming collective accompanied the unveiling.

Recommended

Because reasons.

Because Democracy™.

Via Indy 100 (emphasis added):

A statue of Nelson Mandela has been unveiled in Glasgow, 33 years to the day since he was granted freedom of the city in a packed George Square.

The bronze effigy was unveiled at a ceremony in Nelson Mandela Place on Friday afternoon, with hundreds of people braving the rain to witness the moment.

Mr Mandela became the first black president of South Africa in 1994 after decades of leading the resistance against apartheid in the country, including 27 years in prison. He died in 2013 at the age of 95…

It is the first public monument of a named black person in Scotland.

The ceremony opened with a rousing performance by Glasgow women’s drumming band SheBoom, before speeches from Nelson Mandela Scottish Memorial Foundation chairman Brian Filling and Glasgow Lord Provost Jacqueline McLaren.

Meanwhile, in Glasgow 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁳󠁣󠁴󠁿 A Nelson Mandela statue will be unveiled next week in Nelson Mandela Place, with the project costing hundreds of thousands of pounds. What relevance does he have to Glasgow or Scotland? 🎥 LBC / Glasgow Times https://t.co/ow5OxPmnii

“What on Earth does a South African communist terrorist who died thirteen years ago have to do with Scotland of all places, and why would it warrant a shrine in his honor?” one might ask.

Any meaningful answer, of course, doesn’t exist, which is why the reasons cited are a.) Mandela visited the city once 33 years ago and b.) it symbolizes “the the British people’s solidarity and fierce struggle against the brutal apartheid system.”

Her Grace Lady Ana, depicted above, is the emblem of “born on third base and thought she hit a triple,” in that her Black Power-inspired stance of defiance, along with her ostentatious, vaguely African-themed sash, conveys that she really thinks she’s fighting the power.

In reality, of course, the power in the form of the technocratic bureaucratic state that controls all of the countries located with the European Union is what installed her in her position.

So, far from a challenger to The Man, she’s his tool.

And she either doesn’t know it or is shameless enough to go on with the charade.
